_comment: A bump held back on purpose. A hold reads HELD only while the pin is still at `current` AND upstream's newest release is still `latest_reviewed`; anything newer re-raises BEHIND. Drop the row when the bump lands. eco "upstream" holds a scripts/upstreams.json tag_release or commit_head row by its name (current and latest_reviewed are versions, or full SHAs for a commit_head row). eco "plugin" holds a marketplace pin by plugin name: a plain SHA pin holds current = our pin SHA and latest_reviewed = the upstream HEAD SHA; a skill fork with a scripts/plugin-upstreams.json override holds current = synced_base and latest_reviewed = the newest upstream tag. An optional `eligible` field (UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ) is the time a release-age hold ends: from that time scripts/check-plugin-drift.sh reads the row BEHIND again (rows for the npm and gh ecos are read by scripts/upstreams/pin-scan.py, which does not read `eligible`, so they carry none). An unreadable file, row or time reads BEHIND, never HELD. An optional `release` field names the condition that lifts the hold as a token, not prose (e.g. "vm-proof"), so a resolver can read it.
